title: Basquiat: A Quick Killing in Art

description.main: An unauthorized biography of Jean-Michel Basquiat by the journalist Phoebe Hoban, published by Viking in 1998. It follows him from Brooklyn graffiti to the 1980s art market.
description.extended:
An unauthorized biography of Jean-Michel Basquiat that treats his career as a story about the 1980s art market as much as about the painter.

Hoban traces Basquiat from his Brooklyn graffiti days as SAMO to international success, his friendships with Keith Haring and Andy Warhol, and his death from an overdose in 1988 at 27. The book draws on recollections from people close to him, but his estate did not endorse it. Publishers Weekly noted that Hoban could not get permission to reproduce his work, so the 385-page text carries a few pages of plates and no paintings.

Phoebe Hoban is an American journalist. Viking issued the hardcover in August 1998 and Penguin followed with a paperback in 1999 and a revised edition in 2004.

notes: 385 pages plus 8 pages of plates per library records. Other editions: Penguin paperback 9780140236095 (1999); Penguin revised paperback 9780143035121 (2004); Open Road ebook reissue 2016.
